refreshed_qr.note: What the held `display_and_wait` answers when nobody has scanned yet: the same process id and step id, a new payload — and a NEW `txn_id`. The transaction id is re-issued with every step answer, so the next call must echo this one, not the one the start gave.

body.instructions: Scan the QR code with the WhatsApp mobile app to log in

rejected_user_input.note: A phone number the network would not take. The errcode is the connector's own, not a bridgev2 one — so the Gateway must not switch on a closed set of mautrix codes here. Note what follows: this answer DESTROYS the login process. Every later call against it, the step cancel and the process cancel included, was 404 M_NOT_FOUND. There is no retrying a step.

wrong_txn_id.note: The bug of #106: the Gateway invented a transaction id instead of echoing the one the step carried. A 500, not a 4xx.

wrong_step_type.note: The last path segment must be the step's own type.

unknown_process.note: A process the bridge never had, or one it has forgotten — which is what a bridge restart looks like from outside, and what a cancelled process answers.

no_user_id.note: The second bug of #106: the Gateway sent ?user_id= only on the calls that start something, so the step and the cancel got this.

body.error: User does not have login permissions

step_cancel_unsupported.note: POST .../{step}/cancel on a live `display_and_wait` step. The step-cancel endpoint is not usable for a QR flow on either reference bridge; what releases a held request is the *process* cancel.

body.error: Login process does not support cancelling steps

held_request_when_process_cancelled.note: What the held `display_and_wait` request comes back with when the process is cancelled underneath it. Captured on the Signal bridge (the WhatsApp bridge was in use by the deployment's owner); it is bridgev2's own error, not a connector's.

complete.note: NOT CAPTURED. Completing a login needs a human with the account's phone, so no real `complete` answer exists in this fixture set. This body is bridgev2's declared shape (RespLoginComplete: the created login's id and the user login it belongs to) and it is the one remaining unverified shape in the Gateway's bridge facade — see the PR for #106. Treat any mismatch here as the fourth occurrence of the same bug, not as a surprise.
substituted: the whole body: this is a declared shape, not a captured one
